title: Task validity in financial synthetic data
markdown:
## 1 Why better distributional fit may leave task validity unchanged Modern tabular generative models address distinct distributional challenges: **[CTGAN](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.00503)** handles mixed discrete-continuous types, multimodality, and class imbalance via mode-specific normalization and conditional vectors, while **[TabDDPM](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/kotelnikov23a.html)** applies Gaussian and multinomial diffusion to numerical and categorical fields (*[CTGAN](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.00503); [TabDDPM](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/kotelnikov23a.html)*). However, while both learn empirical distributions effectively, **financial task validity requires strict structural invariants that global distributional similarity metrics cannot enforce**: exact accounting identities, chronological ordering of fiscal periods, covenant applicability conditions, and logical consistency between numerical inputs and reference judgments. Consider a failure mode that admits an exact mathematical proof. Valid financial inputs $`x \in \mathbb{R}^d`$ must satisfy $`m`$ linear accounting or ratio identities $`Ax = b`$, where $`A \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times d}`$ has full row rank. The valid population distribution $`P`$ is supported entirely on the affine subspace $`M = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^d : Ax = b\}`$ and has finite second moments. Let the columns of $`N \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times m}`$ form an orthonormal basis for the normal space orthogonal to $`M`$. Suppose a generative model captures $`P`$ tangential to the manifold but adds a tiny amount of independent noise in the normal directions: $`X_\sigma = X + \sigma N \varepsilon`$, where $`\varepsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I_m)`$ is independent of $`X \sim P`$. Writing the generated distribution as $`Q_\sigma`$, we have for every $`\sigma > 0`$: $$ W_2(P, Q_\sigma) \le \sqrt{E\|X_\sigma - X\|^2} = \sigma \sqrt{m} \longrightarrow 0 \quad (\text{as } \sigma \to 0^+) $$ $$ P(M) = 1, \qquad Q_\sigma(M) = 0 $$ $$ \|P - Q_\sigma\|_{\text{TV}} := \sup_B |P(B) - Q_\sigma(B)| = 1 $$ The first line follows from the coupling $`(X, X_\sigma)`$ constructed on the same probability space. The second follows because $`AN`$ is invertible and a continuous $`m`$-dimensional Gaussian vector equals zero with probability zero. The third follows by taking the Borel set $`B = M`$. Thus, **the 2-Wasserstein distance $`W_2(P, Q_\sigma)`$ can converge to zero while the acceptance rate under exact business constraints remains identically zero ($`Q_\sigma(M) = 0`$) and Total Variation distance remains at its maximum of $`1`$**. This counterexample dictates how responsibilities must be partitioned in a production synthetic data architecture (*[SDV constraint-augmented generation](https://docs.sdv.dev/sdv/modeling/constraint-augmented-generation-cag)*): • **Copula models and conditional sampling** capture cross-sectional rank and tail dependencies across continuous corporate indicators (company scale, operating history, leverage, and margin ratios) so columns are never generated independently. • **[CTGAN](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.00503) and [TabDDPM](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/kotelnikov23a.html)** model complex mixed-type and multimodal empirical distributions, followed by explicit business-rule validation. • **Deterministic variable transformations and manifold projections** enforce hard accounting equalities, ratio bounds, and chronological sequences exactly. ## 2 Enforce business constraints while preserving the correct conditional distribution Enforcing hard constraints by generating unconstrained candidates and discarding violations (post-hoc rejection sampling) becomes computationally intractable as multiple financial constraints tighten simultaneously. Suppose a candidate draw has $`m`$ standardized constraint residuals that behave as independent standard normal variables, and each must lie within a tight tolerance $`[-\epsilon, \epsilon]`$. The acceptance probability and expected candidate draws required per valid input are: $$ \alpha_m(\epsilon) = [2\Phi(\epsilon) - 1]^m \sim \left( \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \epsilon \right)^m \quad (\epsilon \to 0^+), \qquad E[N_{\text{attempts}}] = \frac{1}{\alpha_m(\epsilon)} $$ Each additional accounting or ratio constraint multiplies the expected candidate count. Setting each tolerance to $`\epsilon = 0.05`$ residual standard deviations yields the following exact analytical scaling:
Simultaneous Constraints ($`m`$)Rejection Sampling Acceptance Rate $`\alpha_m(\epsilon)`$Expected Candidate Draws per Valid Input
**1**3.9878%25.08
**2**0.1590%628.84
**4****0.0002529%****395,442.59**
Generating directly through the degrees of freedom permitted by the constraints eliminates these wasted draws. In the linear Gaussian regime, covariance-weighted affine projection also preserves the exact theoretical conditional distribution. For a Gaussian copula, this result applies only when the constraints are affine in its latent Gaussian coordinates; nonlinear marginal transformations do not generally preserve affine constraints in the observed financial variables. Let the initial unconstrained draw be $`Z \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu, \Sigma)`$ with $`\Sigma \succ 0`$. Rather than overwriting a single balance-sheet line item (which corrupts covariance structure), we apply a **covariance-weighted Mahalanobis projection**: $$ X = \arg\min_{x : Ax = b} \frac{1}{2}(x - Z)^\top \Sigma^{-1}(x - Z) = Z + K(b - AZ), \qquad K = \Sigma A^\top (A \Sigma A^\top)^{-1} $$ The first-order Lagrangian stationarity condition is $`\Sigma^{-1}(X - Z) + A^\top \lambda = 0`$; substituting $`AX = b`$ and eliminating the multiplier $`\lambda`$ yields the closed-form update. Since $`AK = I_m`$, every draw satisfies $`AX = b`$ exactly, with mean and covariance: $$ E[X] = \mu + K(b - A\mu) $$ $$ \operatorname{Cov}(X) = (I - KA)\Sigma(I - KA)^\top = \Sigma - \Sigma A^\top (A \Sigma A^\top)^{-1} A\Sigma $$ Because an affine transformation preserves Gaussianity, these moments match the exact regular conditional Gaussian law of $`Z \mid AZ = b`$ (*[Majumdar and Majumdar on Gaussian distributions under linear conditioning](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.09285)*). In our synthetic verification benchmark, generating **200,000 synthetic 12-dimensional financial vectors under 4 simultaneous linear constraints** achieved a **maximum absolute constraint residual of $`1.21 \times 10^{-14}`$** and a **relative Frobenius covariance error of 0.662%** against the theoretical conditional covariance—using direct constrained draws without post-hoc rejection. The nearly 400,000 candidate count above belongs to the separate standardized-residual rejection model. Fields fully determined by accounting definitions are computed analytically; range bounds and chronological date orderings that admit bijective transformations (such as log-transforms or positive increments $`t_{k} = t_{k-1} + \exp(\xi_k)`$) are enforced in latent generation space. ## 3 Use decision margins to determine when reference judgments must be recomputed Synthetic expansion of a golden financial case often preserves the qualitative business narrative while perturbing decisive financial figures, covenant thresholds, or macroeconomic inputs. **Retaining the original golden-case reference answer after perturbing the numbers injects systematic label corruption into post-training**, even when every synthetic input satisfies all accounting constraints. Just as *[FinQA](https://aclanthology.org/2021.emnlp-main.300/)* pairs financial questions with executable reasoning programs, synthetic preference engineering requires the link between inputs, reference conclusions, and expert preference explanations to update dynamically (*[FinQA](https://aclanthology.org/2021.emnlp-main.300/)*). Consider a formal decision rule for choosing between two corporate actions. Let $`d(x)`$ denote the net valuation or metric advantage of Action A over Action B, so the true reference decision is $`\operatorname{sign} d(x)`$. If $`d`$ is $`L`$-Lipschitz on a feasible neighborhood, a sufficient condition for retaining the original reference decision without recomputation is that the perturbation $`\Delta`$ remains strictly within the decision margin: $$ |d(x + \Delta) - d(x)| \le L\|\Delta\|, \qquad |d(x)| > L\|\Delta\| \implies \operatorname{sign} d(x + \Delta) = \operatorname{sign} d(x) $$ Because our diagnostic tasks deliberately target **contested decision boundaries** where models are most prone to error, $`|d(x)|`$ is intentionally small! We can derive the exact closed-form rate of **stale-label error** for a linear comparison rule $`d(x) = w^\top x - c`$ with initial margin $`\gamma = d(x) > 0`$. Under a feasible manifold perturbation $`\Delta \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \Omega)`$ with projected variance $`s^2 = w^\top \Omega w > 0`$, the probability that retaining the original decision reverses the true ground-truth label is: $$ \Pr\{d(x + \Delta) < 0\} = \Pr\{w^\top \Delta < -\gamma\} = \Phi\left(-\frac{\gamma}{s}\right) $$ Verified across $`1,000,000`$ Monte Carlo draws: • When the margin-to-noise ratio $`\gamma / s = 2`$, the inherited-label error rate is **2.28%**. • When $`\gamma / s = 1`$, the inherited-label error rate jumps to **15.87%**. • Near diagnostic decision boundaries where $`\gamma / s = 0.25`$, **40.13% of retained labels are false!** This analytical result explains why our pipeline links case expansion directly to reference recomputation and fresh **five-level pairwise preference grading** (see the later methodological comparison in *[HelpSteer2-Preference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.01257)*). Whenever a synthetic perturbation crosses or approaches a decision boundary, the reference solution is recomputed, fresh candidate model trajectories are sampled, and domain experts evaluate the pair on our five-level preference scale—explicitly annotating which trajectory identified the flipped decisive variable and supported its judgment with primary evidence. ## 4 Define the information available for each temporal task While cross-sectional corporate comparisons do not require continuous-time stochastic processes, dynamic financial tasks—such as derivatives valuation, interest-rate term-structure interpolation, and multi-period liquidity stress testing—require path generators. In these temporal regimes, we deploy **stochastic differential equations (SDEs)** and **neural SDEs** to model path distributions beyond single-time marginals (*[Neural SDEs as Infinite-Dimensional GANs](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v139/kidger21b.html)*), alongside **Brownian bridges** and **stochastic interpolation** (aligning with classical MathWorks stochastic interest-rate path constructions) when conditioning on known intermediate observations or endpoints. However, path conditioning introduces a severe **temporal evaluation leakage hazard** whose magnitude can be derived in closed form. Consider a scaled Brownian motion $`X_u = \sigma W_u`$ over $`s < t < T`$. Under squared error loss, the optimal squared-error predictor acting at time $`s`$ with access only to the historical filtration $`\mathcal{F}_s`$ has conditional mean squared error $`\sigma^2(t - s)`$. If a synthetic pipeline conditions path generation on the future terminal endpoint $`X_T`$ and inadvertently exposes that conditioned structure to a forecasting task, Gaussian conditioning gives (*[Pitman on the Brownian bridge](https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~pitman/s205s03/b_bridge.pdf)*): $$ \operatorname{Var}(X_t \mid \mathcal{F}_s) = \sigma^2(t - s) $$ $$ \operatorname{Var}(X_t \mid \mathcal{F}_s, X_T) = \sigma^2(t - s) - \frac{[\sigma^2(t - s)]^2}{\sigma^2(T - s)} = \sigma^2(t - s)\frac{T - t}{T - s} $$ When $`t = (s + T)/2`$ is the midpoint of the forecasting horizon, conditioning on $`X_T`$ halves the conditional variance, producing an **apparent 29.29% reduction in RMSE** ($`1 - 1/\sqrt{2}`$) that is 100% attributable to future information leakage rather than model capability! (By contrast, if the task explicitly supplies both endpoints $`X_s`$ and $`X_T`$ and asks the model to audit an *interpolation* or back-cast an intervening accounting period, Brownian bridge conditioning is mathematically appropriate.) Our task environment specification therefore enforces a strict separation across three information sets: 1. **Construction Information ($`\mathcal{F}_{\text{gen}}`$)**: Complete paths, terminal endpoints, or latent parameters used by the generator to synthesize the scenario. 2. **Permitted Predictor Filtration ($`\mathcal{F}_s`$)**: The exact historical information legally visible to the model at decision time $`s`$. 3. **Evaluation & Oracle Information ($`\mathcal{F}_{\text{eval}}`$)**: Realized post-$`s`$ outcomes reserved strictly for scoring or explicitly disclosed oracle baselines. ## 5 Test independent execution through Batch Zero and retain the task family as a statistical unit Even when constraint projections, decision-margin recomputations, and filtration rules are mathematically sound, a post-training specification must remain reproducible when executed by hundreds of external specialists. To solve this organizational scaling bottleneck, I created **Batch Zero**: • **The Batch Zero Protocol**: Prior to launching scaled vendor production (*Batch One*), a select cohort of doctoral-level domain specialists with proven delivery records independently executed the entire specification—authoring seed cases, running synthetic expansions, verifying reference solutions, and assigning five-level pairwise preference scores. Every failed case or inter-expert disagreement in Batch Zero triggered surgical revisions to prompt instructions, boundary definitions, and calibration rubrics. Following the pilot’s use in preparing external vendor workflows, **the partner foundation model company adopted Batch Zero as a standard pre-scaling gate across other new post-training tracks**. Simultaneously, our statistical governance prevents **synthetic sample-size overstatement**. Suppose $`G`$ independent golden-case families are each expanded into $`k`$ synthetic variants ($`Gk`$ nominal records), where any two variants within a family share correlation $`\rho`$ and common variance $`\sigma_Y^2`$. Expanding the covariance sum for the sample mean yields the exact **effective sample size** $`N_{\text{eff}}`$: $$ \operatorname{Var}(\bar{Y}) = \frac{Gk\sigma_Y^2 + Gk(k - 1)\rho\sigma_Y^2}{(Gk)^2} = \frac{\sigma_Y^2}{Gk}[1 + (k - 1)\rho] \implies N_{\text{eff}} = \frac{Gk}{1 + (k - 1)\rho} $$ With $`G = 100`$ independent families, $`k = 20`$ synthetic variants per family ($`2,000`$ nominal tasks), and within-family correlation $`\rho = 0.5`$, **the nominal 2,000 records provide the exact same statistical precision for the mean as just $`190.48`$ independent records**—and ignoring within-family correlation understates standard errors by a factor of **$`3.24\times`$**! Consequently, our production pipeline enforces strict family-level train/evaluation splits and computes all confidence intervals with family-level and expert-level hierarchical clustering. ## 6 Establish whether the complete method justifies scaled production To evaluate whether our constraint-preserving synthesis and preference architecture justifies scaled production, we hold the task mix, generator training budget, expert review budget, and final acceptance criteria fixed, introducing each methodological layer in staged blind comparisons evaluated across independent task families:
Comparison StageMethodological Upgrade IntroducedCore Research & Production Question
**Existing production baseline**Unconstrained generation + manual expert review & reworkWhat is the true fully-loaded cost per finally accepted, valid case?
**Add manifold-constrained generation**Fix generator; enforce affine projections & variable transformsDo invalid candidates and manual expert repairs drop while preserving conditional distributions?
**Add margin-aware reference recomputation**Recompute reference judgments when the sufficient Lipschitz margin check fails; use $`\gamma/s`$ to quantify Gaussian label-flip riskDo stale-label errors decline, producing valid supervision on both sides of decision boundaries?
**Apply complete Batch Zero & filtration criteria**Jointly check $`\mathcal{F}_s`$ timing conditions and independent executionDo post-training gains persist after excluding leakage and clustering by source family?
Because raw acceptance rates reward generating trivial variants of easy templates, and raw generation speed ignores manual expert repair costs, we govern production decisions via **Scenario-Weighted Family Coverage Efficiency**. Let $`j`$ index predefined cells in the financial capability matrix with strategic weights $`w_j \ge 0`$ ($`\sum_j w_j = 1`$) and required independent valid family counts $`n_j^* > 0`$: $$ \operatorname{Coverage} = \sum_j w_j \min\left(1, \frac{n_j^{\text{valid}}}{n_j^*}\right), \qquad \operatorname{Efficiency} = \frac{\operatorname{Coverage}}{C_{\text{generation}} + C_{\text{review}} + C_{\text{rework}} + C_{\text{adjudication}}} $$ Once a cell reaches its target $`n_j^*`$ independent families, repeatedly expanding easy templates yields zero marginal coverage gain (*[Alaa et al. on synthetic data evaluation](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v162/alaa22a.html)*). Together, manifold constraint enforcement, decision-margin label recomputation, temporal filtration isolation, and **Batch Zero** calibration establish a rigorous engineering standard for synthetic preference data in frontier model post-training.
